subject: Singificant QTLs from multiple scan but not single QTL scan

messages.author: 4c1c6fa8c6a481c7
messages.subject: Singificant QTLs from multiple scan but not single QTL scan
parts:
Hi,
Is it possible to have no significant QTLs identified from a single QTL scan, but have signficant QTLs identified from a multiple scan?
Thanks,
Cynthia

messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Singificant QTLs from multiple scan but not single QTL scan
parts:
It's possible, but I've not seen it happen, myself.

I'd more often see a single strong-effect QTL in the single-QTL scan, and then after controlling for that I'll find good evidence for further loci.

And sometimes there are important interactors, or pairs of loci linked in repulsion, that aren't seen in the single-QTL scan.

karl

messages.author: 4c1c6fa8c6a481c7
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Singificant QTLs from multiple scan but not single QTL scan
parts:
Thank you for your answer. Can you direct me to which tools I can use to identify interacting QTL?
I'm currently trying to identify QTLs from an F2 population generated from a recombinant congenic strain. The phenotype is normally distributed and I've spaced 34 markers in the recombinant regions to get an initial idea of which recombinant region is most associated with the phenotype. From there I was planning on doing finer genotyping in the QTL containing recombinant regions to narrow the QTL size. 
Single QTL analysis gave me the attached plot. Since the LOD scores are not significant, I was thinking that maybe there are loci that are not significant on their own but are significant when in interaction. Does this make sense?
Thanks,
Cynthia

messages.author: 32b9d1bc3db229a5
messages.subject: Graph in R
parts:
Hi everyone,

This is not strictly an RQtl question but I would like to plot a graph with upto 3 data values per point.

For e.g, the x axis is the lod score
The size of the dot represents 3 frequency values; 33, 67 and 100. The 33 value is represented by largest data point (circle), medium for 67 and smallest for 33 (Frequency)
Then finally the colour of the circle which represents another value between 1000-0. For example if my value is between 0-100 yhe graph plot is shown in red, if between 101-200 then orange .. And so on in 100 step increments.

I'm hoping to flag up markers with high number of missing values on the same graph represented by datapoint

I'm not able to find this information online and was wondering if it is possible with R. If so any pointers or guidelines would be most appreciated.

Thank you and kind regards

Eiram

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Singificant QTLs from multiple scan but not single QTL scan
parts:
If there are gaps > 5-10 cM between markers in the region, the evidence for linkage or for interaction could improve by adding more markers. But once you're down near 5 cM spacing, there won't be much to gain by adding more markers unless the QTL effect is quite large. You gain more by increasing the size of the cross.

karl
